- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1347-1395 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `git_subcommands()` parses nested shell scripts without stripping data heredoc bodies, so a bare guarded git command inside a non-shell heredoc can be incorrectly detected.
  WHY: Unlike `_guarded_git_invocations`, recursive `git_subcommands()` calls do not apply `_strip_data_heredoc_bodies`, causing false-positive blocks or confirmation prompts.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: docstring of `_wrapped_shell_text` at lines 666-668; changelog.d/6777-nested-heredoc-wrapper-check.md:3 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The docstring and changelog incorrectly claim the segment parser drops data heredoc bodies, although `git_subcommands()` does not strip them.
  WHY: Maintainers may rely on this inaccurate description and repeat the false-positive behavior when calling `git_subcommands()` with raw heredoc-laden text.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

The new test at tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:2929 only exercises the second claim with `print('git push origin x')` instead of a bare `git push origin x`.

The diff has 4 changed files; none of them contain a fix to `git_subcommands` or a bare-body regression test.
